reasoning.Sources: The original paper clearly specifies the underlying physical model (RSJ junction model, Eq. 1) and all relevant parameters (hysteresis parameter β, pulse repetition frequency Ω, pulse width p, amplitude of rf bias arf, integration time, time step). The reproduction report, written by the original author, confirms these specifications and details the exact parameter ranges used for each figure, leaving no ambiguity regarding the initial conditions or research questions.
reasoning.Methods: The original paper specifies the numerical method (fourth-order Runge-Kutta) and mentions analog simulations. The reproduction report details the Fortran program's role in solving the differential equation and the Visual Basic program's role in analyzing the I-V characteristics. However, the original paper lacked sufficient detail on the specific implementation of the I-V characteristic calculation and step width extraction, which required the reproducer (the original author) to reverse-engineer their own 25-year-old code. The challenges in porting the Fortran code (proprietary directives, filename handling) and recreating the Visual Basic 1.0 environment (emulator setup, proprietary binary format) indicate that an independent implementation would have been difficult without significant inference or direct access to the original source code.
reasoning.Experiments: The original paper provides clear experimental parameters (e.g., β, Ω, p, arf ranges, integration time, time step) for both numerical and analog simulations. The reproduction report meticulously details the original computational environment (Fortran 5.1 on PCs/DEC workstations, Visual Basic 1.0 on Windows 3.11) and the steps taken to recreate it for the reproduction (gfortran on macOS, Windows 3.11 emulator for Visual Basic). The specific ranges and increments for arf are explicitly stated for each pulsed drive simulation. The successful reproduction of the figures, confirmed by the author, indicates that the experimental configurations and protocols were sufficiently specified to allow for independent reconstruction, albeit with the challenge of legacy software.
